items.title: Calculation of Relative Molecular Mass (Mᵣ) of a Gas (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Calculation of Relative Molecular Mass (Mᵣ) of a Gas: a main subheading of 5.2 Ideal gas equation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 97-97.

blocks.text: Agar gas ka P, T, V aur grams mein mass maloom ho to equation (4) se us ka relative molecular mass nikal sakte hain. Is ke liye equation (4) ko thora badalte hain.
Equation (4) mein n = m/M rakhein, jahan m = grams mein mass aur M = gas ka molar mass:
Ab equation (5) ko M ke liye hal karein:
Molecular level par molar mass hi relative molecular mass ban jata hai, is liye:

blocks.title: Sample Problem 5.1
blocks.problem: 134 g gas ka volume -73 ℃ aur 10 atm pressure par 5 dm³ hai. Gas ka relative molecular mass maloom karein.
steps: Formula: M = mRT/PV. Pehle temperature ko kelvin mein badlein: T = -73 + 273 = 200 K.
M = (134 g)(0.0821 atm dm³ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)(200 K) / (10 atm)(5 dm³)
blocks.answer: Gas ka relative molecular mass 44 hai (kitab ise 44 amu likhti hai).

blocks.title: Easy words mein
blocks.text: Har sawal mein pehle °C ko K mein badlein (273 jama karein), aur R = 0.0821 ke saath pressure atm mein aur volume dm³ mein rakhein. Units kat kar sirf g mol⁻¹ bachta hai.

blocks.prompt: a) Gases asani se compress kyun ho jati hain?
blocks.explanation: Gas ke molecules ek doosre se bohat door hain aur gas ka taqreeban 99.9% volume khali jagah hai. Dabane par molecules sirf is khali jagah mein qareeb aa jate hain, is liye gas asani se dab jati hai.
Jab compressed gas ko achanak phailne (expand hone) diya jaye to woh thandi ho jati hai. Achanak phailne par yeh thandak Joule-Thomson effect kehlati hai.

blocks.prompt: c) 21 g gas ka volume -90 ºC aur 7 atm par 8 dm³ hai. Relative molecular mass nikalein.
blocks.explanation: T = -90 + 273 = 183 K. M = mRT/PV = (21 × 0.0821 × 183) / (7 × 8) = 315.5 / 56 = 5.6 g mol⁻¹. Relative molecular mass taqreeban 5.6 hai.

items: Boyle (V ∝ 1/P), Charles (V ∝ T) aur Avogadro (V ∝ n) mil kar PV = nRT dete hain; R = 0.0821 atm dm³ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
n = m/M rakhne se Mᵣ = mRT/PV; Sample Problem 5.1 ka jawab 44.
